chapter: Nola band, day job and nightclub work
title: The Nola Band, Ernest Johnson's band, Jack Carey and Punch Miller
summary: Henry Rush was in the Nola Band; LaCaze stayed six to eight months with Ernest Johnson, then started the Nola Band, and played often with Jack Carey.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Did Russ play with your band? Russ, yeah, yeah. You mean the Supreme Band possibly?
No, Lola, we had a band called the Lola Band. That was with Eddie Jackson too. Eddie Jackson was a manager with my college, you know.
But anyway, you went to Duck Owners, and how long did you stay with anything?
Oh, I stayed with them for, I might say quite a few months, maybe six, eight months, maybe.
Well, I can't remember where I went from Duck Owners. I don't remember.
But sometime after that you started the Lola Band then?
Yeah, yeah, sometime after that we started the Lola Band. That was the next band you had? I don't remember. I can't remember. Who was with Duck Owners in those days?
Who was the trumpet player before you? Before me, I don't remember.
Or after, huh? I can't even remember that. Yeah, yeah.

I know some people that played with him, you know, but it's hard for me to remember too, because Dave Bailey used to tell me all about that band. Yeah, yeah. And then Punch used to play with him at one time too, both of you. Punch Miller. Yeah.

Yeah, he played with him, he played with him quite a bit. And just, well that's different, he used to trombone player. Jack Carey, Punch Miller played with him quite a bit too. I played with Jack Carey myself quite a bit, but we never had an organized band, you know. But he would always, as much as possible, pick me to do the job whenever he had one.
